messages.subject: Cross type for Brem et al. dataset?
messages.subject_clean: Cross type for Brem et al. dataset?
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to analyze data generated in the paper:

The landscape of genetic complexity across 5,700 gene expression
traits in yeast
Rachel B. Brem*,† and Leonid Kruglyak*,‡

Here they simply crossed two haploid yeast lines and genotyped the F1
generation.
Which cross type should I use? Are there special steps needed to
analyze a haploid species?

Thanks for all the great work!

messages.subject: comparing r/qtl to multiQTL
messages.body_plain:
I've been mapping with MultiQTL but switched to r/qtl recently because
I have one binary trait (which MultiQTL can't deal with).   I think
I've been running r/qtl correctly but I can't recreate the results I
got for the other, normally distributed traits analyzed with the
MultiQTL software.  Has anyone else tried to compare these two
programs?  I know they run different algorithms but I expected to get
somewhat similar results for the normally distributed traits.  Another
little wrinkle...I have an outcrossed mapping family but I am
analyzing the sexes separately so have been using the backcross model
in both MultiQTL and r/qtl.  Not sure if that would affect the
comparisons between programs though.

thanks

Erin

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] comparing r/qtl to multiQTL
messages.body_plain:
You don't give us too much to go on.  Just how different are the
results?
It's hard to say, without looking at the results and the data, why the
programs are giving you different answers.

I'm not sure how you would analyze the outcross data as two separate
backcrosses; I've seen that done for genetic map construction, but for
QTL mapping it seems (to me) a bit odd.

regards,
karl

messages.subject: How to carry out locus interaction and covariates in "2part" model?
messages.subject_clean: How to carry out locus interaction and covariates in "2part" model?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I have dataset with phenotype as "2part" model.

First question. Is there any way to do locus interaction in scantwo
for "2part" model. Manual says scantwo is only appopriate for normal
and binary dataset.

Second question is still about the distribution requirement. Can I do
analysis of covariates for "2part" phenotype in the model? Does it
also ask for normal or binary distribution?

If answers to above two questions are "No". Could you recommendate a
way to deal with "2part" phenotype? Or just tell me which softwares
are available for that.

Many thanks

Young

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to carry out locus interaction and covariates in "2part" model?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] How to carry out locus interaction and covariates in "2part" model?
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl doesn't have facilities for doing scanone with covariates or
scantwo with the two-part model, at this point.  Such things are
certainly appropriate, they just aren't implemented.

The best thing to do would be to separate the binary trait from the
conditional quantitative trait, and analyze the two parts separately
with scanone with covariates and/or scantwo.

Regards,
karl

messages.body_plain:

I am trying to run fitqtl, but I got an error. Suppose I have a set of
data, and the code what I was using is as follow:

>chr = c(2, 2, 11)
>pos = c(10, 70, 20)
>qtl = makeqtl(data.sim, chr, pos)
>my.formula = y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q1:Q2
>out.fitqtl = fitqtl(data.sim, qtl=qtl, formula=my.formula)

But I got an error message like:

Error in as.double.default(pheno) : (list) object cannot be coerced to
'double'

Does any one can help figuring out what the problem is?

Thanks!

PR
